bkr__1.why: hmi answers dbd's owner queries in its own thread instead of only between its gateway sends, so the hmi->gw->dbd->hmi cycle no longer deadlocks; dbd still asks the owner on a cache miss.

bkr__2.why: dbd replies a constant 1 for every non-preloaded key instead of asking the owner (hmi), so the cycle is gone but the lookup answer is invented.

bkr__3.why: Only lengthens hmi's receive window; hmi still listens only after its send to gw returns, and that send waits on dbd, which waits on hmi.

bkr__4.why: Raises hmi's priority to 30; the send/receive cycle hmi->gw->dbd->hmi is unchanged.

cnu__1.why: Each stage receives and acks upstream frames in a separate thread while the main loop pushes downstream and waits on a semaphore, so the three-stage ring of send-first stages no longer deadlocks and frames still flow.

cnu__2.why: Puts 50 ms send/reply and receive timeouts around the ring exchange, so stages time out and tick without frames actually being handed over.

cnu__3.why: Staggers the start of each stage by a few ms; every stage still sends downstream before receiving, so the ring deadlocks as before.

cnu__4.why: Only sets the stage priority to 12; all three stages still send first and block in the ring.

cv4__1.why: The HEADER request moves to its own thread signalled by a semaphore, so the event thread keeps answering catalogd's visibility queries while HEADER waits for a free worker; both refreshes finish and the header is still fetched.

cv4__2.why: Adds a third catalogd worker on the same channel, so HEADER is served while the two REFRESH workers are waiting on the ui event thread, which then gets its reply and answers them; all requests are still made and answered.

cv4__3.why: The ui event thread never sends the HEADER request any more (flag just cleared), so the header fetch after a refresh is skipped and the deadlock cannot form.

cv4__4.why: catalogd workers no longer ask the ui whether the entry is visible and use a hard-coded on=1, so the visibility check is invented.

epe__1.why: keys replies to auth before re-registering with the broker, so the broker is free to receive the registration; the ui->broker->auth->keys->broker cycle is broken and the registration still happens.

epe__2.why: Wraps the route registration in a 30 ms send/reply timeout, so keys gives up on the blocked broker and the re-registration is silently lost.

epe__3.why: keys no longer opens or contacts the broker at all; the route re-registration after rotation is removed.

epe__4.why: Only raises the broker's priority to 20; the circular send chain through keys back to the broker is unchanged.

f82__1.why: eeprom's channel is created without _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY, so its page read inherits the caller's priority (bus at 14 / pilot at 35) and the priority-12 scrubber can no longer starve it; the full pilot->bus->eeprom path is kept.

f82__2.why: Only raises the eeprom server from 4 to 20, above the scrubber; the only functional change is a message receiver's priority.

f82__3.why: Shortens the busy page read to 5 ms, but eeprom still runs at fixed priority 4 below the always-running scrubber at 12, so it never gets CPU.

f82__4.why: bus no longer forwards to the eeprom server and replies with a locally computed word, so pilot gets an answer that was never read from the device.

g6b__1.why: pwrmgr now replies (empty) to the keep-alive message, so hmi's MsgSend returns and the keep-alive is still recorded.

g6b__2.why: hmi sends the keep-alive as a pulse, but pwrmgr's loop drops pulses (rcvid==0 -> continue), so the keep-alive is sent where nobody handles it and last_keepalive is never updated.

g6b__3.why: A separate thread prints hmi TICKs every 100 ms while the real loop still blocks forever on the unanswered keep-alive.

g6b__4.why: pwrmgr holds the keep-alive to answer with the next setpoint, but the only client is hmi, which is blocked on that keep-alive and never sends another setpoint.

grp__1.why: imud's channel no longer uses _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY, so fusion runs at fc's priority 32 and logfmt at 16 can't starve it; fc still gets real attitude samples.

grp__2.why: Only raises the imud server from 6 to 18, above logfmt; the only change is a message receiver's priority.

grp__3.why: logfmt appends fake 'TICK grpfc' lines to fc's log while fc itself stays blocked on the starved imud.

grp__4.why: fc's request to imud gets a 150 ms send/reply timeout, so fc ticks without receiving attitude data while imud is still starved.

k74__1.why: audiod handles the QD_VOLUME message (sets master volume and replies) and MsgErrors other unknown types, so the player is answered and the volume is actually set.

k74__2.why: audiod answers the unknown volume message with ENOSYS, so player unblocks but the master volume request is rejected and never applied.

k74__3.why: player never sends the master-volume message (if (0 && ...)), so the work that hung is skipped.

kk5__1.why: The flusher thread receives on int_chid, the channel the writer sends flush requests to, so each flush is served and the writer waits for it as designed.

kk5__2.why: The flush request becomes a pulse to int_chid, which nobody receives on, so the writer no longer waits and no page is ever flushed.

kk5__3.why: The writer no longer sends a flush request and instead writes the flusher's TICK lines itself, faking flush activity that never happened.

kk5__4.why: ConnectAttach with getpid() instead of 0 names the same process, and the flusher still receives on ext_chid, so the writer's flush send still blocks forever.

kp6__1.why: On a compaction commit the store compacts and then replies to the pending writer instead of dropping its rcvid, so the writer is acked after the journal holds its value.

kp6__2.why: On compaction the pending write is kept (and not journaled twice), so the next commit pulse acks the writer as the original comment intended.

kp6__3.why: Writes are acked immediately on receipt instead of after the commit pulse journals them, so the writer no longer waits for durability; the ack no longer means committed.

kp6__4.why: Only rewrites compact() to guard against jlen overflow; compaction still clears pending_write without replying, so the writer stays blocked.

nrp__1.why: jobc answers jobd's commit confirmation in a dedicated receiver thread, so the confirmation arrives while the main thread waits on the commit submit; two-phase commit is kept.

nrp__2.why: jobd's phase-2 confirmation send gets a 20 ms timeout, so the commit is acknowledged without the client ever confirming.

nrp__3.why: jobd drops phase 2 entirely and never contacts the client's notification channel, so commits are acked without confirmation.

nrp__4.why: Adds a third jobd worker, but the worker serving a commit still sends to the client's channel while that client is blocked waiting on the same worker's reply.

p5u__1.why: rated decrements inflight after each completed request and replies EBUSY to shed callers, so the counter no longer leaks and ctl gets real conversions (or retries on EBUSY).

p5u__2.why: Shed callers get EBUSY instead of being left blocked, but inflight is still never decremented on success, so after six requests every request is shed and ctl's loop never ticks again.

p5u__3.why: ctl no longer opens or sends to rated; the result is computed locally and thrown away, so the server is cut out of the loop.

p5u__4.why: A timer callback prints ctl TICKs every 100 ms, and the TICK is removed from the real loop, which still blocks on the shed request.

qgj__1.why: The CRC scrubber runs in 5 ms slices with 10 ms sleeps instead of spinning forever at 15, so the fixed-priority ADC server at 5 gets CPU and ctl gets real conversions; the scrub keeps running, at a lower rate.

qgj__2.why: Only raises adcd from 5 to 20, above bgcrc; the only change is a message receiver's priority.

qgj__3.why: The ADC request moves to a sampler thread (which still blocks on the starved adcd), and the control loop ticks on the stale initial value 3300 instead of waiting for a conversion.

qgj__4.why: Shortens the averaging window to 10 ms, but adcd still sits at fixed priority 5 below the spinning bgcrc at 15 and never runs.

zte__1.why: Mergers now receive before sending while collectors still send first, so every send in the four-stage ring has a listening peer and batches keep flowing.

zte__2.why: Collectors now receive before forwarding while mergers still flush first, which breaks the all-send-first ring symmetrically; batches still flow hop by hop.

zte__3.why: A sampling thread prints collector TICKs every 150 ms, and the real hand-over loop (still deadlocked) no longer ticks.

zte__4.why: Collectors hand batches over as fire-and-forget pulses, so they never wait for the merger to accept; the ring runs, but the synchronous one-batch-in-flight hand-over is replaced by an unacknowledged non-blocking send.
